Allen Coral Atlas Class Descriptions

Source: vignettes/aca-classes.Rmd
aca-classes.Rmd

This page provides the full class descriptions and colour schemes used by ReefMappeR for benthic habitat and geomorphic zone mapping, following the Allen Coral Atlas classification system.

Full methodology: allencoralatlas.org/methods

Geomorphic Zones

Value Colour (hex) Class Description
11 #77d0fc Shallow Lagoon A shallow, enclosed or semi-enclosed, sheltered, shallow-bottomed area dominated by sediments.
12 #2ca2f9 Deep Lagoon A sheltered, broad body of water, semi- or fully enclosed by reefs. Variable depth (shallower than surrounding ocean) with soft bottom dominated by reef sediment.
13 #c5a7cb Inner Reef Flat A low-energy, sediment-dominated, horizontal to gently sloping platform behind the Outer Reef Flat.
14 #92739d Outer Reef Flat Adjoins the seaward margin of the reef; a planar, broad and shallow platform with strong wave-driven zonation.
15 #614272 Reef Crest A zone marking the boundary between the reef flat and reef slope. Typically shallow and characterised by highest wave energy absorption.
16 #fbdefb Terrestrial Reef Flat A broad, flat, shallow to semi-exposed area of fringing reef directly connected to land on one side and exposed to freshwater runoff, nutrients and sediments.
21 #10bda6 Sheltered Reef Slope A submerged, sloping area extending into deep water, sheltered from strong directional prevailing wind or current by land or opposing reef structures.
22 #288471 Reef Slope A submerged, sloping area extending from the reef crest (or plateau) toward the shelf edge. Windward-facing or in any direction when no prevailing wind or current.
23 #cd6812 Plateau A deeper, submerged reef feature with hard bottom, oriented horizontally or gently sloping seaward.
24 #befbff Back Reef Slope A complex, inner, often gently sloping reef zone behind the Reef Flat. Variable depth, sheltered, sediment-dominated and often interrupted by coral outcrops.
25 #ffba15 Patch Reef A small, free-standing to semi-free-standing coral reef within a lagoon, rising from a sandy area.

Benthic Habitats

Value Colour (hex) Class Description
11 #ffffbe Sand A soft substrate dominated primarily by fine, unconsolidated sediments.
12 #e0d05e Rubble A habitat of loose, coarse fragments of broken reef material.
13 #b19c3a Rock Any exposed surface of hard, bare substrate.
14 #668438 Seagrass Habitats where seagrass is the dominant biota.
15 #ff6161 Coral/Algae Any hard substrate area where living corals and/or algae are growing.
18 #9bcc4f Microalgal Mats Visible accumulations of microscopic algae within sandy sediments.

Reference

Allen Coral Atlas (2020). Coral reefs of the world. https://allencoralatlas.org

Lyons, M.B. et al. (2020). Mapping the world’s coral reefs using a global multiscale earth observation framework. Remote Sensing in Ecology and Conservation, 6(4), 557–568. https://doi.org/10.1002/rse2.157
